lessons.title: Should for Advice and Expectations
lessons.content: 'Should' is used to give advice, express expectations, or indicate what is right or wrong. The structure is Subject + should + V1.

details.explanation: 'Should' is used to give advice about what is good or bad for someone.
details.burmese: မင်း အရက်မသောက်သင့်ဘူး။

details.explanation: 'Should' is used to say that you expect something to happen.
details.example: There is a traffic jam on this road, you should go by Metro.
details.burmese: ဒီလမ်းပေါ်မှာ ယာဉ်ကြောပိတ်ဆို့မှု ဖြစ်နေတယ်။ မင်း မီတရို စီးသင့်တယ်။

details.explanation: 'Should' can be used to ask for advice or opinion.
details.example: Should I go to the temple on Thursday?

lessons.title: Ought to for Obligation and Duty
lessons.content: 'Ought to' is similar to 'should' but expresses a slightly stronger obligation or moral duty. The structure is Subject + ought to + V1.

details.explanation: 'Ought to' is used to express what is morally right or what someone should do.
details.example: You ought to respect your elders.
details.burmese: မင်း အသက်ကြီးသူတွေကို လေးစားသင့်တယ်။

details.explanation: 'Ought not to' is used to say what someone should not do.
details.example: You oughtn't to ride a motorbike without a helmet.
details.burmese: မင်း ဦးထုပ်မပါဘဲ ဆိုင်ကယ်မစီးသင့်ဘူး။

details.explanation: 'Ought' can be used to ask for advice or confirmation.
details.example: Ought she to call the police?
details.burmese: သူမ ရဲကို ခေါ်သင့်လား။

lessons.title: Should vs Ought to
lessons.content: 'Should' and 'ought to' are very similar in meaning, but there are some differences in formality and strength.

details.explanation: 'Ought to' is more formal than 'should'. 'Should' is more common in everyday speech.
details.example: You should study harder. (less formal) / You ought to study harder. (more formal)

details.explanation: 'Ought to' can express a slightly stronger moral obligation than 'should'.
details.example: You should tell the truth. (advice) / You ought to tell the truth. (moral duty)
details.burmese: မင်း အမှန်တရားကို ပြောသင့်တယ်။ (အကြံပြုချက်) / မင်း အမှန်တရားကို ပြောသင့်ပါတယ်။ (ကျင့်ဝတ်)

details.explanation: 'Should' uses 'shouldn't' while 'ought to' uses 'ought not to'.
details.example: You shouldn't be late. / You ought not to be late.
details.burmese: မင်း နောက်ကျသင့်ဘူး။ / မင်း နောက်ကျသင့်ဘူး။
